page: Google Cloud Platform n1-highcpu-8 is an x86_64 architecture virtual server powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.3 GHz. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, providing 2 threads per core. The system is equipped with 7.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 0.9 GB of RAM per core. It does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPU accelerators, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks place this instance in the weak to average tiers. The single-core and multi-core stress-ng CPU tests register weak performance at 1109.79 and 5820.12 respectively. Memory bandwidth tests show a weak read-only speed of 325.55 GB/sec for small cached blocks, but average performance for large uncached blocks with 47.28 GB/sec read and 34.7 GB/sec write speeds. Cryptographic and compression tasks are generally poor, with single-threaded gzip compression at 19.07 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 7.0 GB/sec. However, the instance achieves average results in Geekbench ray tracing at 6021.0 and PassMark CPU score at 6786.78.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the n1-highcpu-8 offers a low-cost entry point for compute-bound tasks that require multiple dedicated threads but have minimal memory requirements. The low RAM-to-vCPU ratio avoids the expense of unneeded memory capacity. This configuration is suitable for workloads such as light software compilation, basic multi-threaded batch processing, and low-demand web serving where memory overhead is low.
